# Historical iOS build warning dispositions

This inventory uses the four Build job logs from [run 38827436342](https://github.com/eunsoogi/orot/actions/runs/38827436342), attempt 1, at `35d00b0da86b72bc4caf5f4eb00cf36a50b5ea93`. After removing ANSI styling and the Actions job/timestamp prefix, the selector includes case-insensitive `warning:`, standalone `WARN`, CocoaPods `[!]`, and `DVTAssertions: Warning` lines. A standalone `WARN` must be the diagnostic-level token in the normalized log prefix; source text such as `console.warn` and workflow metadata such as `if-no-files-found: warn` are excluded. It drops 59 indented Xcode source-excerpt lines that repeat a diagnostic's `warning:` text. In these logs, the excerpts are marked `|- warning:` or `` `- warning: ``: Debug has 28, Release 15, Production 16, and OAuth none. They comprise 48 Objective-C header excerpts and 11 Swift excerpts. It then groups by producer and warning category. The selected set has 1,518 occurrences in 38 groups: 1,455 primary `warning:` records, 4 Metro `WARN` records, 50 Xcode DVT notices, and 9 CocoaPods script-phase notices. The downloaded logs contain 1,514 raw `warning:` lines because those include the 59 repeated source excerpts. Per-profile selected totals are Debug 556, Release 488, Production 473, and OAuth 1. Normalized classifier output matches every table row's occurrence count and profile split, not only the overall total. Each of the 38 row labels also maps to a producer/category group in the normalized output. Counts are occurrences, not unique defects.

These dispositions describe the #201 candidate against the historical evidence above. The earlier clean-derived-data Debug, Release, Production, and OAuth profile builds used `732191f299c0735d5ee816391323f52872fec807` as `HEAD` and ran from a dirty candidate worktree. That worktree included the warning-related shared-scheme, app `Info.plist`, and generic-destination changes, plus an unrelated `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` formatting edit. The corresponding source inputs are now part of this PR, but those executions are not clean-commit or hosted acceptance evidence. A separate clean-derived-data `OrotMobile` Release app build from source commit `f553e4af` also ran with the app `Info.plist` change and an unrelated `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` formatting edit still unstaged; its original invocation and residual warnings are recorded below, and it is not exact clean-PR-head proof. A current-head four-profile build matrix remains pending after #204 integration. An earlier Release app build preceded the additional `p-queue@6.6.2` and `metro@0.87.1` patches and reported their timer-global and color-environment warnings. Each patch applies to its pinned source, and the WorkerFarm regression reproduces the conflict against unpatched Metro. An isolated patched-worker run preserves `NO_COLOR` and retains Metro's default color override when it is absent. The 14-patch frozen install succeeded, and a current readback confirmed all patch hashes match `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and the installed lock. The focused warning suite passed 21/21 after the bundle-phase regression was added. Before the app bundle-phase edit, a clean-derived-data `OrotTests` Release test-product build also succeeded. `#NoUsage` and the unknown-enum diagnostic remain with #204's owner. The tvOS-only Keychain fallback retains deprecated Security keys without suppression and remains outside these iOS build profiles.

The earlier Debug test-product, Release test-product, and Production app logs contain seven, ten, and nine warning diagnostics; OAuth package and harness logs contain none. Raw `warning:` text matches are 8, 10, and 11 for the three Xcode profiles because the Debug `#NoUsage` and Production `#NoUsage`/unknown-enum diagnostics each have a repeated source excerpt. A separate pre-patch clean `OrotMobile` Release app build contains 14 Xcode warning records: nine RNScreens Objective-C category members, two Hermes timer-global warnings from `p-queue`, the #204-owned unknown-enum diagnostic, an App Intents metadata-extractor notice, and the app bundle script phase. The metadata warning reads `Metadata extraction skipped, no AppIntents.framework dependency found`; a source search found no `AppIntent` or `AppShortcut` declarations in `apps/mobile/` or `packages/`, so retain it as a tool notice for a target with no App Intents integration. During that pre-patch build, Node reported that `NO_COLOR` was ignored because `FORCE_COLOR` was set. Metro 0.87.1's `WorkerFarm` passes `FORCE_COLOR=1` even when `NO_COLOR` is inherited; the new regression reproduces both values reaching its child process. The patch omits Metro's default `FORCE_COLOR` in that case, preserves an explicitly inherited value, and retains Metro's default when `NO_COLOR` is absent. The focused installed regressions passed, and the clean Release app build at executable candidate commit `f553e4af` also passed without the Metro color-environment warning. The earlier clean `OrotTests` Release test-product log contains 13 warning diagnostics: nine RNScreens category-only object notices, three App Intents metadata-extractor notices, and one app bundle script-phase notice. The candidate project marks that phase to run every build while its output list remains empty; the configuration regression and Xcode project syntax check pass. The clean `OrotMobile` Release app build at `f553e4af` confirmed that Metro bundling ran and the bundle-phase no-output warning did not appear. That earlier test-product log contains no p-queue timer-global or Metro color-environment warning. The `#NoUsage` diagnostic appears in the earlier Debug and Production logs. No other historical source-warning group reappeared in the profile logs. The earlier Debug test-product log also contains one unexplained `error:` line stating that a command failed with exit code 0 immediately before the HealthKit fixture compile; the xcodebuild invocation itself returned 0. This non-warning message remains unresolved.

Using the successful Release test product at `/tmp/orot-201-builds-Z8MKxi/release-test/Build/Products/OrotTests_iphonesimulator27.0-arm64.xctestrun` on a fresh iOS 27 iPhone 18 Pro Simulator, the Core state-persistence suite passed 3/3, fixture-isolation passed 2/2, recording-persistence passed 2/2, and Core integration passed 18/18, including both `RecordingMeteringBoundaryTests`. The result bundles and logs are under `/tmp/orot-201-builds-Z8MKxi`; the result parser verified all 18 integration cases, and the task-owned Simulator was deleted afterward. A prior Core UI run did not complete: the recording-export case waited for a background recording row that its second launch did not seed. The unmerged #204 Draft PR contains a fixture correction in `RecordingExportProbeHarness.tsx` and `RecordingExportUITests.swift`; this #201 candidate leaves those owned files untouched. Rerun the UI case after #204 integration. The separate `OrotMobile` Release app build completed successfully before the `p-queue` patch; it is not evidence for the newly patched queue.

The Production app build's 11 `op-sqlite` compile invocations explicitly enable `-Wshorten-64-to-32` and `-Wcomma` after `-Wno-conversion`; neither warning is suppressed in those commands. The four target response files and generated Debug and Release `op-sqlite` target configurations omit `-Wno-comma` and `-Wno-shorten-64-to-32`. Both suppression flags appear in the separate `Pods-OrotMobile` aggregate `WARNING_CFLAGS`, but are not passed to the inspected `op-sqlite` compile commands. The clean Production result therefore reflects the source repairs for these warning families, not suppression of them in the compiled SQLCipher target. This audit predates the `p-queue` change and does not prove that dependency's timer warnings are fixed.

At source commit `f553e4af`, a clean-derived-data `OrotMobile` Release app build with Xcode 27.0, arm64, and `-jobs 2` succeeded from a dirty worktree. The local invocation used `generic/platform=iOS Simulator`; the worktree also contained the unstaged app `Info.plist` removal and unrelated `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` formatting change. It ran the Metro bundle phase from `index.js` and produced `Orot.app/main.jsbundle` (7,592,545 bytes). The raw log has 12 literal `warning:` lines: nine RNScreens category-only libtool notices, one #204-owned `UnavailableReason` switch warning, one App Intents metadata-extraction warning, plus one indented duplicate Swift source excerpt. No p-queue timer-global warning, Metro `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` warning, app bundle no-output warning, or empty location description warning appeared. Xcode emits a note that the bundle phase runs every build because dependency analysis is unchecked. This confirms that one local Release build and bundle output only; it is not a clean PR-head build, does not establish runtime UI behavior, and does not prove the other profiles. The candidate remains incomplete: RNScreens category runtime behavior and the #204-held HealthKit and enum warnings require integration/validation, while the App Intents extractor warning remains a tool diagnostic for a target without App Intents declarations. The issue's 38-category historical count is reconciled, but other profile, UI, authentication, review, and integration requirements remain open.

## Additional local-only candidate change

The preserved 12-patch candidate also patches `jest-worker@29.7.0` so its default child-process environment does not add `FORCE_COLOR` when the parent has `NO_COLOR`. Metro separately supplies its own environment through `forkOptions.env` and explicitly adds `FORCE_COLOR`; its patch removes that caller-provided value when `NO_COLOR` is present. These patches cover different environment inputs. The jest-worker change is outside the 38 groups from the hosted run above. Its earlier local inventory and raw log are not present here, so no occurrence count or before-and-after result is claimed. The current frozen install applied this patch. The real child-process regression passed its `NO_COLOR`, explicit `FORCE_COLOR`, and default-color cases in the focused warning suite.

The additional `p-queue@6.6.2` patch is also outside those historical groups. It changes the pinned queue's `setInterval` and `clearInterval` references to explicit `globalThis` access after the clean Release app bundle reported two undeclared-global warnings in `_initializeIntervalIfNeeded` and `_tryToStartAnother`. The unified patch applies to an isolated copy of the pinned source and produces one `globalThis.setInterval` and two `globalThis.clearInterval` calls. The current frozen install applied it, the focused workspace regression passed, and the Release app log from executable candidate commit `f553e4af` has no p-queue timer-global warning.
The additional `metro@0.87.1` patch is outside the 38 historical groups. Metro's `WorkerFarm` unconditionally adds `FORCE_COLOR=1` to transformer-worker environments, which conflicts with an inherited `NO_COLOR` and produced the Node warning in the pre-patch Release app log. The behavior contract is to omit Metro's default `FORCE_COLOR=1` when the parent supplies `NO_COLOR`, preserve an explicitly inherited `FORCE_COLOR`, and retain Metro's default when `NO_COLOR` is absent. This leaves Node's documented precedence intact when a caller explicitly supplies both values. The non-goal is to rewrite caller-owned environment values or filter the warning; when callers provide both values, any resulting Node warning remains visible. The current frozen install applied the patch, the child-worker regression passed its no-color, explicit-force, and default-color cases, and the Release app log from executable candidate commit `f553e4af` has no Metro color-environment warning. See the [Node.js v22 CLI documentation](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v22.12.0/docs/api/cli.html) for environment-variable precedence.

After the 14-patch frozen install, the installed pnpm lock records `p-queue@6.6.2` at patch hash `4103539d89883652925f16f1ef9d51cb26dcbeb5f91260b7c74306825cf797ab` and `metro@0.87.1` at `aa1d88ca5a5b6791dea24eb7220f8f1f334593112e17446114964dfa2fe7b501`, matching the candidate lock. The clean Release app build at executable candidate commit `f553e4af` also passed and confirmed these warnings are absent and the bundle phase runs; Core UI remains unverified until the #204 UI-test change is integrated.

## Local prebuilt archive comparisons

The comparison was run from worktree head `4289b320`; the prebuilt patch, lockfile, workspace file, and header-preparation helper match their contents at `41cc35d0`. It used the existing local caches and products and did not run a new install, flavor switch, or app build.

On 2026-10-19, the local Debug and Release Core archives were also checked against the SHA-1 sidecars published for the pinned React Native 0.87.1 artifacts on Maven Central. Both values match, and the CocoaPods setup log records successful SHA-1 verification before copying the two archives from the shared cache. The [Debug checksum](https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/facebook/react/react-native-artifacts/0.87.1/react-native-artifacts-0.87.1-reactnative-core-debug.tar.gz.sha1) is `2515f5c73e818e190843b8b9d3827b6b9b27dd7e`; the [Release checksum](https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/facebook/react/react-native-artifacts/0.87.1/react-native-artifacts-0.87.1-reactnative-core-release.tar.gz.sha1) is `2c7b2a03cbae4cdc267f802d9f2711d6e7dcc762`. This confirms byte agreement with those published checksums; it does not validate Apple's code signatures.

- The cached Release archive `reactnative-core-0.87.1-release.tar.gz` has SHA-256 `56c4a9a53a698a9c055262589015963ea521123bee41a4891b9914accd3f308b`. With `.last_build_configuration` set to `Release`, its installed `React.xcframework` matches across all 242 non-header and non-module-map files. The comparison includes three framework executable slices and six `_CodeSignature` files, with no missing, extra, or mismatched files.
- The cached Debug archive `reactnative-core-0.87.1-debug.tar.gz` has SHA-256 `ac8ff0e90096acaae396dd513b76aad8efaac91a81656f2d8dbd82bf84588821`. Its simulator `React.framework` slice matches the existing Debug simulator build intermediate across all 78 non-header and non-module-map files, including the executable and resource seal.
- The existing Debug app-embedded framework differs from that intermediate in only `React` and `_CodeSignature/CodeResources`. The intermediate executable contains arm64 and x86_64 slices; the app-embedded executable contains one arm64 slice, and both report the same arm64 Mach-O UUID. The arm64 data before the code-signature payload matches byte-for-byte after excluding the `__LINKEDIT` and code-signature size fields in the load commands. The signature data offset is `69643936` in both files, while its size changes from `562368` to `136304`; the resource seal's `files2` dictionary lists 75 entries in the app embed and none in the intermediate. The legacy `files` dictionaries list 76 and one entry, respectively, with `Info.plist` accounting for the difference. This explains the observed local byte differences as architecture packaging and signature metadata changes. A strict verification of the embedded signature was not completed, so this does not establish signature validity.

These comparisons and checksum checks establish local consistency for the named files and byte agreement with Maven Central's published SHA-1 values. They do not establish cold-cache installation reproducibility or Apple code-signature validity; the embedded Debug signature has not passed strict verification. The clean current-head profile matrix and remaining native and authentication checks also remain open until #204 integration and return of the shared Xcode and Simulator slot.
